claims.text: Under fixed OER conditions, high-entropy perovskite oxides exhibit higher catalytic activity than conventional single-B-site perovskites.
Synergistic interactions among multiple transition-metal cations create dynamic mixed oxidation states.
Dynamic mixed oxidation states tune the d-band centers of the catalyst.
Tuning the d-band centers optimizes adsorption and desorption kinetics of OER intermediates.
Epitaxial LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3–δ films have spatially heterogeneous oxidation states.
Pulsed laser deposition on identical substrates ensures identical and uniform surface facets for the compared films.
High-entropy perovskite films form and dynamically evolve mixed oxidation states and local electronic heterogeneity during OER.
Multication interactions dynamically adjust the d-band center.
Multication-induced changes in intermediate adsorption and desorption kinetics cause improved OER activity relative to conventional single-B-site perovskites.
High-entropy perovskite films may produce a 17–680-fold increase in current density at fixed overpotential relative to conventional films.
Operando spectroscopy will reveal oxidation-state shifts that correlate with enhanced catalytic performance.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to epitaxial perovskite films made by pulsed laser deposition under controlled aqueous OER conditions.
Non-epitaxial synthesis or drastically different testing environments may alter the proposed mechanism.
The magnitude of activity improvement and the contribution of individual cations depend on synthesis and testing conditions.
